verdicts.note: Attacked on magnitude: the Chamber Q&A hedges to 'without unnecessary tax increases' [S2]. But the pamphlet is categorical: 'We're taxed enough already—I have never voted for or supported the annual 1% property tax increase' and 'without raising taxes' [S1]. S2 adds pushing back on state taxes that burden rural businesses. Opposing even the routine 1% levy increase is the pole. Two independent sources: -2 high holds.

Attacked on direction: he backs public-private partnerships, business incentives and tourism promotion [S2] and proposes federal payments to counties for set-asides [S3], which lean toward investment. But his budget statements are restraint-first: 'fiscal discipline to fund public safety and services' and budgets that prioritize core services [S1][S2]. He proposes no audit or cut agenda, so -1, not -2. Medium holds.

Attacked on direction: zoning previously unzoned Underwood land at 10-acre lots [S4] is low-density and arguably restrictive, not a supply push. But in context it opened about 400 acres to residential use over unanimous public opposition, and he argued for it as diversifying land use [S4]. He frames developable land, not public investment, as the housing constraint [S2] and has no public-housing, rent or tenant position. -1 medium holds. Wording nit: the basis says the vote was to 'rezone' forest land; S4 describes zoning previously unzoned land.

Attacked as off-axis: legacy-forest opposition [S5] and roadside logging [S3] are framed as timber revenue and fire breaks, not climate policy. The one on-axis statement is that he will fight for policies that 'reduce energy costs' [S2], which matches pole_a's label, but he says nothing on carbon pricing, the CCA or energy sources. Indirect inference: -1 low (excluded from alignment math) is the right treatment.

Attacked on magnitude: he has served one term (elected 2022 [S7]), not long tenure. But he is the sitting commissioner and board chair [S3][S4], has a voting record [S4][S5] he runs on, and makes no outsider pitch; pole_a is incumbency itself. -2 high holds.

Attacked toward 0: he cites 'management experience' and school board service [S1], and S2 confirms he was a White Salmon Valley School District director in 2009. But he has held no county office, this is his first county run [S1], and his pitch is 'we need new leadership and innovative ideas' against the sitting chair [S1]. Prior school board service keeps it at +1 rather than +2. Medium holds: the evidence is pamphlet-only, but the statement is explicit.

note: Missing scores considered and not proposed: Mosbrucker on housing and spending (he names housing scarcity and school cuts as problems but offers no remedy [S1], as his dossier notes), Mosbrucker on taxes (no evidence), Leckie on reform (his 'straightforward, populist' self-description [S1] and mini PDC reporting [S8] say nothing about PAC money or structural reform, and his WSAC role [S2] is not evidence either way), Leckie on safety ('fund public safety' [S1][S2] has no enforcement-vs-prevention direction). His push-back on state mandates [S2] is local-control evidence, and that axis does not apply to County contests. Display review: office_does matches contest S2-S5. race_blurb matches contest S1, S3, S4 and S6 and is neutral. Leckie's summary and five highlights match S1-S5 and S7; 'board chair' is documented for Dec. 2025 and Mar. 2026 [S3][S4]. Mosbrucker's summary and four highlights match S1, S2, S4 and S5.
